title: L3: drop the ignored obsidian_vault_path setting from the lead-finder settings API and page

Observation files are written to a server-managed vault folder for this organization.

title: L4: tell users which SMTP ports and TLS modes are accepted, at the form and in the send error
interface:
The allowed SMTP ports are 25, 465, 587 and 2525 (lib/email/account-validation.ts SMTP_PORTS) and sendViaSMTP sets requireTLS when `secure` is false, so a relay that does not offer STARTTLS fails. Surface this in three places, with the literal string `Allowed ports: 25, 465, 587, 2525. Port 465 uses TLS; the other ports require STARTTLS.` in each (do not import it from lib/email/account-validation, that module pulls node:net into a client bundle). app/dashboard/settings/client.tsx: in the custom-account form, directly after the closing `` of the `grid grid-cols-2 max-sm:grid-cols-1 gap-4` that holds the SMTP Host / Port / Username / Password inputs (the block under the `Outgoing (SMTP)` label, around line 3085-3110) and before the `smtp_secure` checkbox label, add `

Allowed ports: 25, 465, 587, 2525. Port 465 uses TLS; the other ports require STARTTLS.

`. app/dashboard/campaigns/client.tsx: directly after the closing `` of the two-column grid that holds the SMTP Host and Port inputs (around line 270-282, inside the `provider === "custom_imap"` block), add the same `

...

` line. lib/email/sender.ts sendViaSMTP: replace the error string `Mail server not allowed` with `SMTP host or port not allowed. Allowed ports: 25, 465, 587, 2525. Port 465 uses TLS; the other ports require STARTTLS.` (this string is what lands in email_accounts.last_error, so existing accounts on a rejected port explain themselves). No other behaviour changes.

title: L6: page the guest cleanup scan so permanently skipped rows cannot stall it
interface: lib/auth/guest-cleanup.ts adds `export const GUEST_CLEANUP_MAX_PAGES = 5`. purgeExpiredGuests keeps its signature and return shape and now scans in pages: each page is the existing profiles query (same select, `.like` and `.lt` filters, `.limit(GUEST_CLEANUP_BATCH)`) plus `.order("id", { ascending: true })`, and every page after the first adds `.gt("id", <id of the last row of the previous page>)`. Each page goes through selectExpiredGuests (unchanged signature and cap) and the existing per-row loop (unchanged logic, counters and error strings). Scanning stops after a page that returned fewer than GUEST_CLEANUP_BATCH rows, after GUEST_CLEANUP_MAX_PAGES pages, or on a scan error (pushed to `errors` as `scan: <message>` exactly as today, then return). `scanned` is the total across pages. tests/guest-cleanup.test.ts keeps every existing test and adds a `purgeExpiredGuests` describe using a hand-rolled fake admin client (a chainable query builder object that records the calls made on it and resolves to a page per call; do NOT mock @supabase/supabase-js): (a) the first profiles page returns GUEST_CLEANUP_BATCH rows (all `is_anonymous: false` from `auth.admin.getUserById`) and the second page returns one anonymous guest row with an organization_id whose other-member count is 0; `organizations.delete` and `auth.admin.deleteUser` resolve `{ error: null }`; expect `scanned` = GUEST_CLEANUP_BATCH + 1, `skipped` = GUEST_CLEANUP_BATCH, `deletedUsers` = 1, `deletedOrgs` = 1, `errors` = [], and that the second profiles query called `.gt("id", <id of the 200th row>)`; (b) a fake that always returns a full page of non-anonymous rows stops after GUEST_CLEANUP_MAX_PAGES pages: `scanned` = GUEST_CLEANUP_BATCH * GUEST_CLEANUP_MAX_PAGES; (c) a scan error on the first page yields `errors` = ["scan: boom"] and `scanned` = 0. Rows in the fakes must satisfy selectExpiredGuests (guest emails, created_at older than 7 days relative to the `now` passed in).

title: RLS: mirror the admin/owner server-action gates on the account tables (migration 031) and gate the OAuth connect callbacks
interface: Today email_accounts (016 policy "org_email_accounts"), whatsapp_accounts ("whatsapp_accounts_org_scope") and linkedin_accounts ("linkedin_accounts_org_scope") each have one FOR ALL policy keyed on org membership only, so the requireRole('admin','owner') gates in lib/actions/email-accounts.ts (addCustomEmailAccount, deleteEmailAccount), lib/actions/campaigns.ts (createEmailAccount, deleteEmailAccount) and lib/actions/whatsapp-accounts.ts / linkedin-accounts.ts (disconnect*, delete*) do not hold for direct PostgREST calls. supabase/migrations/031_account_role_rls.sql, idempotent and in the same header/comment style as 030_followup.sql (numbered header, 'Apply by hand in the Supabase SQL editor', DROP POLICY IF EXISTS before every CREATE POLICY): for each of the three tables drop the FOR ALL policy named above and create per-command policies named `<table>_select`, `<table>_insert`, `<table>_update`, `<table>_delete`. Define org membership as `organization_id IN (SELECT organization_id FROM public.profiles WHERE id = auth.uid())` and admin as `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.profiles WHERE id = auth.uid() AND role IN ('admin','owner'))`. SELECT: USING (member). UPDATE: USING (member) WITH CHECK (member). DELETE: USING (member AND admin) on all three tables. INSERT: WITH CHECK (member AND admin) on email_accounts (mirrors addCustomEmailAccount / createEmailAccount and the OAuth callbacks gated below); WITH CHECK (member) on whatsapp_accounts and linkedin_accounts because connectWhatsAppAccount and saveLinkedInAccount are not role-gated in code. The header comment lists this mapping, notes that service-role writers (cron routes, lib/email/sender.ts, lib/whatsapp/sender.ts, lib/linkedin/*) bypass RLS and are unaffected, and ends with verification queries (as comments) that select from pg_policies for the three tables. No other tables. app/api/email/oauth/google/callback/route.ts and app/api/email/oauth/microsoft/callback/route.ts: the profile select becomes `.select("organization_id, role")`; directly after the existing `if (!profile?.organization_id) { redirect("/dashboard/settings?error=no_org"); }` add `if (!hasRequiredRole(profile.role)) { redirect("/dashboard/settings?error=forbidden"); }` with `import { hasRequiredRole } from "@/lib/auth/roles";`. This runs before the token exchange. Nothing else in either route changes. Open-access guests are admins of their own workspace (lib/auth/guest-workspace.ts sets role 'admin'; 030 backfills sole members), so guest flows are unaffected.

title: Review fix H1/L3: protect email_accounts credential columns at the database and gate updateEmailAccount
interface: Migration 031 is not applied anywhere yet, so it is edited in place. (1) Append a section `(B) email_accounts credential columns: admin/owner only` with `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.protect_email_account_credentials() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public` in exactly the shape of 028's protect_profile_tenant_columns: when any of NEW.smtp_config, NEW.imap_config, NEW.oauth_tokens, NEW.provider, NEW.email_address, NEW.organization_id IS DISTINCT FROM the OLD value, AND `auth.role() IS NOT NULL AND auth.role() <> 'service_role'`, AND `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.profiles WHERE id = auth.uid() AND role IN ('admin','owner'))`, RAISE EXCEPTION 'mail account credentials can only be changed by an organization admin' USING ERRCODE = '42501'; otherwise RETURN NEW. Then `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS protect_email_account_credentials ON public.email_accounts;` and `CREATE TRIGGER protect_email_account_credentials BEFORE UPDATE ON public.email_accounts FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.protect_email_account_credentials();`. Member-level status / is_default / tracking_domain / last_error / daily_send_limit / display_name / signature_html updates keep working; lib/email/sender.ts and the cron routes write through service_role and are unaffected. (2) `whatsapp_accounts_insert` and `linkedin_accounts_insert` change from member-only to member AND admin (`role IN ('admin','owner')`), because connectWhatsAppAccount and saveLinkedInAccount insert through createAdminClient (RLS is bypassed there), so no application path used the member-level INSERT. Rewrite the header comment that currently says those two functions 'are not role-gated' to state this reason instead. (3) Add the trigger to the header's Fixes list and a commented verification query on pg_trigger (`SELECT tgname FROM pg_trigger WHERE tgrelid = 'public.email_accounts'::regclass AND tgname = 'protect_email_account_credentials';`). Keep the file idempotent. lib/actions/email-accounts.ts updateEmailAccount: replace `const orgId = await getOrgId();` with the same requireRole("admin", "owner") try/catch + unstable_rethrow gate that deleteEmailAccount in this file uses, returning the same error shape it returns, and use the gate's orgId. Everything else in the function (the mail-config checks, the update query, stripMailSecrets) is unchanged. getOrgId stays imported because other functions use it.

title: Review fix M1/L4/L5: correct the SMTP TLS help text, default secure off for 587, derive secure for 465 in the campaigns modal, surface OAuth errors
interface: TLS mode comes from smtp_config.secure (lib/email/sender.ts: `secure`, `requireTLS: !secure`), not from the port, so the O2 wording was wrong. app/dashboard/settings/client.tsx: (a) the help text under the SMTP grid becomes `Allowed ports: 25, 465, 587, 2525. Tick the SSL/TLS box below for port 465; leave it unticked for the other ports (STARTTLS).`; (b) both places that default the custom form's `smtp_secure: true` (the initial useState default near line 2840 and the reset near line 2897) become `smtp_secure: false` (the default port is 587, which is STARTTLS); imap defaults are untouched; (c) in the useEffect that reads `searchParams.get("connected")` (near line 2857), after the `if (connected) {...}` block add: `const oauthError = searchParams.get("error"); if (oauthError) { setToastMessage(oauthError === "forbidden" ? "Only organization admins can connect email accounts" : \`Email connection failed: ${oauthError}\`); setToastVariant("error"); setShowToast(true); }`. app/dashboard/campaigns/client.tsx: the help text becomes `Allowed ports: 25, 465, 587, 2525. Port 465 uses SSL/TLS; the other ports use STARTTLS.` and loses its `mt-2` class (the fragment made it a direct child of the space-y-4 container); the smtp_config object sent on save becomes `{ host: smtpHost, port: parseInt(smtpPort), secure: parseInt(smtpPort) === 465 }`. lib/email/sender.ts sendViaSMTP: the rejection string becomes `SMTP host or port not allowed. Use a public mail server on port 25, 465, 587 or 2525.` (it is also returned when DNS resolution fails, so it no longer claims to describe TLS). Nothing else changes.
